---
title: "Secrets and Sensitive Ground"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
**Prerequisites:** Rules of the Carapace. **Objective:** keep keys, settings and sensitive data out of the agent's reach, and know what changes on a shared cluster.
**Time:** about 15 minutes. <span class="ao-badge">General practice, not a vendor claim. Your own data agreement and cluster policy override anything here.</span>
:::

Most of this team's data is not sensitive. Some of it is, and then special agreements apply. This quest does not use any real data. It is about **habits**, so that the careful choice is automatic.

## Three ideas

1. **A prompt leaves your machine.** Anything an agent reads may be sent to a model provider. Treat "the agent can read it" as "it may leave here". Whether that is allowed for your data is decided by your agreement, not by convenience.
2. **Secrets are not content.** API keys, tokens, SSH keys and passwords belong in a secret store or environment variable that the agent has no permission to read. Do not paste them into a chat or into an instructions file you commit.
3. **A shared cluster is shared.** What is fine on your laptop can disturb other people on a login node, or break a data policy on shared storage. Cluster rules apply to agents exactly as they apply to you.

::: {.callout-note}
In the Crypt you already learned deny rules. A deny on your secrets files is the armour for idea 2. See *Rules of the Carapace*.
:::

## Honour-system side quest

Nobody checks this and nothing depends on it. It is only here because the real rules are in a document you have and I do not.

<div data-ao-honour="find-agreement" data-xp="20">Find the data-handling agreement or policy that applies to your project (or ask your group leader where it is). Read the passages about <strong>where data may be processed</strong> and <strong>whether it may be sent to external services</strong>, and write down in your own notes what they say.</div>

<div data-ao-honour="find-secrets" data-xp="10">List where your own API keys and settings files live (for example a <code>.env</code> file or a shell profile), and check that your agent's permission rules deny reading them.</div>
